metadata.title: Combine, Don't Pick.
metadata.subtitle: The Knowledge-Synthesis Skill (Multi-Source Search)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude answers from several overlapping search results, does it just pick the best one? Lands the carry-out that the skill combines every source, weighed by freshness and authority, with every surviving claim traced back to where it came from.

beats.narration_text: Give Claude a handful of search results, and you might think it just picks the one best result and stops there. It doesn't pick — it combines. So: does Claude just combine the best sources?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is knowledge-synthesis, and it has one job: turn scattered search results into a single answer. The SKILL.md lays out the work as steps, and Claude runs them in order — gather the results, then combine them. Linear, start to finish, unless a step says otherwise.

Here's what combining actually means. Feed it results from several sources that overlap, and it doesn't stack them end to end. It merges the repeated claims into one, drops the duplicates, and keeps a record of exactly which source each surviving claim came from — so you can trace any line in the answer back to where it was said.

production_viz.label: DEDUPE, THEN ATTRIBUTE
production_viz.caption: every line traces to its source

beats.narration_text: When two sources disagree, the skill doesn't just average them. Each claim gets weighed by two things — how recent the source is, and how authoritative it is — and the higher-weighted claim wins the sentence. Run the same sources through it twice and you get the same answer both times: the weighing follows the rule every time, not a mood.

production_viz.label: WEIGHED, NOT AVERAGED
production_viz.caption: same input, same weights, same output

beats.narration_text: The skill never picks a winning source — it combines every one of them, weighed by how fresh and how authoritative each is, and it always tells you which source each claim came from.

props.quote: The skill never picks a winning source — it combines every one of them, weighed by how fresh and how authoritative each is, and it always tells you which source each claim came from.
props.sparkLine: Combine, weigh, attribute. Never just pick.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I have three write-ups on the same topic that overlap and disagree in a few places. Read all three, combine what's true across them into one answer, remove anything repeated, and for each claim you keep, tell me exactly which write-up it came from and why you trusted it over the others where they disagreed. Then check what comes back: does every claim carry a source, and does it explain the call it made when two write-ups disagreed?
